obligations.expected_behavior: The artifact contains exactly three primary examples.
forbidden_result: The primary example set contains fewer or more than three examples.
obligations.observable_result: A validator counts three primary examples.
obligations.state_after: The primary example set has exactly three members.
obligations.state_before: The authored artifact is being checked for compliance with SM-A07.
obligations.subject: Primary example count
obligations.trigger: When the primary examples are authored or validated.

obligations.expected_behavior: The three primary examples are arranged in the declared order.
forbidden_result: The primary examples appear in the wrong order.
obligations.observable_result: The primary sequence is ordered as required.
obligations.state_after: The primary examples are in the required order.
obligations.state_before: The primary examples exist but their ordering is being validated.
obligations.subject: Primary example ordering
obligations.trigger: When the primary examples are authored or validated.

obligations.expected_behavior: The primary examples cover the typical, boundary, and error routes.
forbidden_result: Any of the typical, boundary, or error routes is absent from the primary set.
obligations.observable_result: Each of the three route categories is represented by a primary example.
obligations.state_after: Typical, boundary, and error route coverage is present in the primary set.
obligations.state_before: Route coverage of the primary examples is being validated.
obligations.subject: Primary route coverage
obligations.trigger: When the primary examples are authored or validated.

obligations.expected_behavior: Every primary example has a nonempty Input.
forbidden_result: A primary example has missing or empty Input.
obligations.observable_result: Input is present and nonempty for all three primary examples.
obligations.state_after: All primary examples contain nonempty Input values.
obligations.state_before: The primary examples' Input fields are being checked.
obligations.subject: Primary example Input
obligations.trigger: When each primary example is authored or validated.

obligations.expected_behavior: Every primary example has a nonempty Output.
forbidden_result: A primary example has missing or empty Output.
obligations.observable_result: Output is present and nonempty for all three primary examples.
obligations.state_after: All primary examples contain nonempty Output values.
obligations.state_before: The primary examples' Output fields are being checked.
obligations.subject: Primary example Output
obligations.trigger: When each primary example is authored or validated.

obligations.expected_behavior: Each primary example is tied to a distinct declared branch ID.
forbidden_result: Two primary examples use the same branch ID.
A primary example references a branch ID that is not declared.
obligations.observable_result: All primary examples reference declared branch IDs and no two references are identical.
obligations.state_after: Each primary example has a unique declared branch ID.
obligations.state_before: Branch-ID associations for the primary examples are being validated.
obligations.subject: Primary example branch identity
obligations.trigger: When each primary example is authored or validated.

obligations.expected_behavior: Each primary example is tied to its expected result.
forbidden_result: A primary example lacks an expected result association.
obligations.observable_result: Every primary example has an explicit expected result tied to it.
obligations.state_after: Expected results are associated with all primary examples.
obligations.subject: Primary example expected results
obligations.trigger: When each primary example is authored or validated.

obligations.expected_behavior: When supplemental examples are present, they do not change the primary example set.
forbidden_result: Supplemental examples are counted as primary examples or otherwise change the primary set.
obligations.observable_result: The primary set remains the same three ordered examples regardless of supplemental references.
obligations.state_after: Supplemental examples, if any, remain outside the unchanged primary set.
obligations.state_before: Supplemental examples may exist in references while the primary set is being evaluated.
obligations.subject: Supplemental example isolation
obligations.trigger: When supplemental examples are included in references.

obligations.expected_behavior: Validation fails when an example has a missing or empty Input/Output pair.
forbidden_result: A missing or empty Input/Output pair is accepted as valid.
obligations.observable_result: The validator reports failure for the missing or empty pair condition.
obligations.state_after: The invalid example set is rejected for the missing or empty pair.
obligations.state_before: A candidate example contains a missing or empty Input/Output pair.
obligations.subject: Missing or empty pair rejection
obligations.trigger: When validation encounters a missing or empty Input/Output pair.

obligations.expected_behavior: Validation fails when the primary examples are in the wrong order.
forbidden_result: A wrongly ordered primary set is accepted as valid.
obligations.observable_result: The validator reports failure for the wrong-order condition.
obligations.state_after: The wrongly ordered primary set is rejected.
obligations.state_before: The primary examples are arranged in an order that violates the requirement.
obligations.subject: Wrong-order rejection
obligations.trigger: When validation detects an incorrect primary example order.

obligations.expected_behavior: Validation fails when primary examples use a duplicate branch ID.
forbidden_result: A duplicate branch assignment is accepted as valid.
obligations.observable_result: The validator reports failure for the duplicate-branch condition.
obligations.state_after: The primary set with a duplicate branch ID is rejected.
obligations.state_before: At least two primary examples use the same branch ID.
obligations.subject: Duplicate branch rejection
obligations.trigger: When validation detects duplicate branch IDs among primary examples.

obligations.expected_behavior: Validation fails when a primary example references an unknown branch ID.
forbidden_result: An unknown branch ID is accepted as valid.
obligations.observable_result: The validator reports failure for the unknown-branch condition.
obligations.state_after: The primary set with an unknown branch reference is rejected.
obligations.state_before: A primary example references a branch ID absent from the declared branch IDs.
obligations.subject: Unknown branch rejection
obligations.trigger: When validation detects an undeclared branch ID.

obligations.expected_behavior: Validation fails when normalized Input and Output are identical across examples that have different labels.
forbidden_result: Examples with identical normalized Input/Output and different labels are accepted as valid.
obligations.observable_result: The validator reports failure for the identical-normalized-Input/Output condition with different labels.
obligations.state_before: Two or more examples have identical normalized Input/Output but different labels.
obligations.subject: Identical normalized pair rejection
obligations.trigger: When validation detects identical normalized Input/Output values paired with different labels.
